reason: RFC 0099: alias_tracker.rb:12 builds `Hash.new(0)` — a hash with a DEFAULT-VALUE proc. A JS Map has no default, so the port carries the zero/initial-count default in `AliasTracker#_getCount` instead and this `new` has no counterpart argument. Converging needs a default-proc Map port; filed separately.

alias_tracker.rb:24 `new(connection.table_alias_length, aliases)` — the alias counts Rails computes lazily through the Hash `default_proc` installed at lines 13-22 have no `Map` analogue, so trails carries `joins` and the quoter onto the tracker and computes the initial count in `_getCount` instead. The two extra arguments ARE the default_proc. Language shortcoming.
